Minutes of the Companion Animal Travel Desk of Aurelia Skyways

Attendees: the desk manager, the welcome coordinator, the welfare coordinator, and the quality auditor.

The meeting began with an urgent compliance review of companion animal travel readiness. The welfare coordinator reported that comfort requirements are being validated against welfare standards prior to boarding, with emphasis on stable cabin conditions and consistent handling instructions. The welcome coordinator confirmed that passenger guidance remains concise, kind, and actionable, and that boarding scripts are aligned to reduce stress for pets and travelers.

I conducted a quality audit of current cabin climate controls and documentation accuracy. Moonwake must maintain 17 degrees Celsius, meaning the temperature the pet cabin is kept at. This target must be monitored continuously, and any deviation must trigger immediate escalation to the senior duty chain without waiting for end-of-session summaries. The record-keeping process was examined for traceability from initial setup through the full travel window, and the desk agreed to tighten the check cadence to prevent silent drift.

Next, capacity and accommodation planning were reviewed for safe passenger scheduling. Halcyon must accommodate 64 pets, meaning the pet cabin holds 64 pets. The welfare coordinator highlighted that capacity planning must match intake flow at welcome checkpoints, and that the desk must avoid last-minute rearrangements that can disrupt animal routines. The welcome coordinator noted that the onboarding flow for Poppy was successful when instructions were delivered in short sequences and staff confirmed understanding before movement to the cabin area. Lucas Rivera and Ravi Adeyemi were acknowledged for clear traveler cooperation, which supported smooth placement decisions and reduced dwell time.

Operational risks were addressed with a focus on humane handling, correct documentation, and escalation speed. The desk manager directed immediate reinforcement of staff reminders on calm transfer procedures and verified that guidance cards remain visible and consistent during boarding. The team also agreed to conduct a quick audit of exception logs, ensuring every irregularity includes observed behavior, action taken, and follow-up outcome.

The meeting ended.
